items.question: Place the following European explorers in chronological order: Christopher Columbus, Marco Polo, Vasco Nuñez de Balboa. Why are each of these explorers important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Polo, Columbus, Balboa. Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant who traveled to China in the late 1200s. When Polo’s account of his voyage was published many years later in 1477, it spurred European desires to find a way to the rich markets of the Far East. Looking for Asia by sailing west across the Atlantic, Columbus instead discovered a New World in 1492.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper decade. Events: The Spanish conquest of Mexico The Portuguese explorations of the African coast and discovery of the Cape of Good Hope The Spanish conquest of Peru The first exploration of Christopher Columbus Spanish expeditions into the American Southwest Decades: 1480–1490 1490–1500 1520–1530 1530–1540 1540–1550
items.answer: Portuguese mariners were exploring the Atlantic coastline of Africa in the 1480s. In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias discovered the Cape of Good Hope. Columbus first reached the western hemisphere in 1492. Hernando Cortès captured the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan in 1521. This broke the power of the Aztec empire and secured his conquest of Mexico.

items.question: How does the nineteenth-century American historian see the conquistador Hernando Cortés? Is his assessment fully positive or negative?
items.answer: Prescott’s The History of the Conquest of Mexico combines excellent scholarship with a nineteenth-century Romantic sensibility that makes it a dramatic and colorful narrative. Prescott admires Cortès and sees him as a great Romantic hero, bending events to his will. However, as a nineteenth-century man, Prescott deplores the conquistador’s cruelty and religious fanaticism.

items.question: Place the following terms in chronological order: encomienda, astrolabe, Crusades Why are each of these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Crusades, astrolabe, encomienda. The Crusades were religious wars waged by Christian Europeans in the Middle Ages. The Europeans hoped to stop Islamic territorial advances and to win back control of the Holy Land. The astrolabe was a navigational device that helped European mariners calculate their latitude.

items.question: What is Las Casas’s argument? What would he have thought of the behavior of Spanish settlers in the New World?
items.answer: Bartolomé de Las Casas was a Dominican friar who opposed the mistreatment of Native Americans and in person and in print defended their humanity and rights. While Las Casas had some influence on government policy, his attitudes had little impact on most Spanish settlers. Aside from converting Native Americans to Christianity, the settlers were intent on using conquered peoples as a source of labor.

items.question: What does the Castillo de San Marcos tell you about Spanish settlement in the New World?
items.answer: The Castillo de San Marcos is an imposing edifice that tells someone looking at it that the Spanish came to stay in America. The Castillo also tells the observer that the Spanish settlers lived in a dangerous world. The Castillo was attacked several times over the years. The Castillo is the oldest surviving masonry fort in the continental United States.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper decade: Events: The English and French establish their first permanent colonies in North America. The Pilgrims and Puritans settle in Massachusetts. Maryland is founded by the Calvert family. Pennsylvania is founded by William Penn. The first colonial legislature meets in Virginia. Decades: 1600–1610 1610–1620 1620–1630 1630–1640 1680–1690
items.answer: The English settled Jamestown in 1607. This was the first successful English colony in America. Samuel de Champlain founded the French settlement of Quebec in 1608. The Virginia House of Burgesses, the first colonial legislature, began meeting in 1619. The Pilgrims landed at Plymouth in 1620. The Puritans established the Massachusetts Bay Colony in 1629. The first settlers arrived in Maryland in 1634.

items.question: How did the Spanish, French, and English differ in their treatment of Native Americans? Give examples to illustrate the differences.
items.answer: All Europeans, whatever their nationality, regarded the Native Americans as heathen barbarians. The Spanish attempted to convert the Native Americans to Christianity, and then integrate them as workers in the colonial economic and social structure. Examples would be the encomiendas of early Spanish settlers and the missions established by the Franciscans and other religious orders in the Southwest and California.

items.question: Place the following European explorers in chronological order: Robert La Salle, Henry Hudson, Jacques Cartier. Why are each of these explorers important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Cartier, Hudson, and La Salle. Jacques Cartier made three voyages to Canada in the 1530s and 1540s, exploring the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the St. Lawrence River. His voyages helped lay the foundation for New France. Henry Hudson was an English sea captain working for the Dutch East India Company. In 1609, Hudson explored Manhattan and the river that would be named after him.

items.question: What was the purpose of the first Thanksgiving? How has the meaning of the holiday changed over time?
items.answer: The first Thanksgiving took place in November 1621, when the Pilgrims, with some Wampanoag Indian guests, celebrated a good harvest after the hardships that they had suffered in their first year in America. Thanksgiving did not become a national holiday until 1863, following a proclamation by President Abraham Lincoln.

items.question: What point is Williams making in this passage? Why is this important for American history?
items.answer: Roger Williams was a Puritan minister and theologian who came to believe that church and state should be separated. His criticism of the Puritan establishment in Massachusetts led to the colony’s authorities ordering his banishment in 1635. In 1636, Williams and some followers established a new settlement at Providence in what became the colony of Rhode Island. Settlers here were assured freedom of conscience.

items.question: Place the following figures from seventeenth-century English colonial history in chronological order: Anne Hutchinson, John Smith, Squanto. Why are each of these people important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is John Smith, Squanto, Anne Hutchinson. John Smith was the military man whose leadership contributed to the survival of the English colony at Jamestown, Virginia. He claimed that after being captured by Native American members of the Powhatan Confederacy, his life was saved by Pocahontas, the daughter of their chief. Squanto was a member of the Patuxet tribe.

items.question: Distinguish between Roman Catholicism, the Church of England, and Puritanism. How did these influence English colonization in America?
items.answer: Roman Catholicism was the Christian church of Europe before the Reformation. The clergy of the Church were organized hierarchically, with the Pope at their head. Roman Catholicism emphasized regular attendance at the Mass and other liturgies, sacraments, and the performance of good works as a means to salvation. King Henry VIII created the Church of England when he broke with the Catholic Church in the 1530s.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper decade: Events: King George’s War The beginning of the Great Awakening King William’s War Queen Anne’s War The Stono Rebellion Decades: 1690–1700 1700–1710 1720–1730 1730–1740 1740–1750
items.answer: King William’s War began in 1688 and raged until 1697. In Europe it was known as the War of the League of Augsburg. Queen Anne’s War began in 1702 and ended in 1713. In Europe it was known as the War of the Spanish Succession. The religious revival of the Great Awakening began in the 1720s and lasted into the 1740s. The Stono Rebellion, a slave uprising in South Carolina, took place in 1739.

items.question: The dramatist Arthur Miller wrote his play The Crucible (1953) about the Salem Witch Trials as a commentary on the anti-Communist fears of the Second Red Scare. At one point, the play’s protagonist declares: Why did Miller see a similarity between the Salem Witch Trials and the Second Red Scare? Why does he have his protagonist condemn himself as well as his judges?
items.answer: Arthur Miller saw the Salem Witch Trials and the Second Red Scare as comparable because he believed both were hysterical reactions against imaginary threats. He opposed the investigations of the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) into the political beliefs of filmmakers, writers, and actors.

items.question: Place the following events in English political history in chronological order: the Acts of Union between England and Scotland, the Glorious Revolution, the English Civil War. Why are these events important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is the English Civil War, the Glorious Revolution, and the Acts of Union between England and Scotland. The English Civil War lasted from 1642 to 1651 and resulted in the execution of King Charles I and the establishment of a Puritan dictatorship under Oliver Cromwell.

items.question: What does Westover tell you about the life of a wealthy planter family in Virginia in the eighteenth century?
items.answer: The Byrd family’s mansion of Westover was built around 1750. It is a magnificent example of Georgian architecture. Westover testifies to the wealth of some Virginia planters. It also testifies to the high level of culture of some planters; the Byrd library was once one of the largest in America.

items.question: What is the difference between mercantilism and free trade? What are some examples of mercantilism in action in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries? Who was the greatest eighteenth-century British advocate of free trade?
items.answer: Mercantilism was an economic theory that encouraged governments to increase their share of limited global wealth by maintaining a favorable balance of trade. This was accomplished by regulations that encouraged exports while restricting imports from foreign countries with high tariffs. Colonies provided raw materials and staple products that were turned into finished goods by the mother country. The greatest eighteenth-century British advocate of free trade was Adam Smith, whose The Wealth of Nations (1776) argued that free markets and the division of labor create national wealth.

items.question: Thomas Bacon was a minister in Maryland. What point is Bacon making to his congregation? What does this tell you about the attitudes of some colonists in eighteenth-century Maryland?
items.answer: Bacon was telling his congregation of African American slaves that they should accept their station in life. They were to perform their duties willingly and without complaint. They were to do this because their station in life was the will of God and to object would be to defy God’s authority.

items.question: Place the following figures into chronological order: Nathaniel Bacon, Jonathan Edwards, Sir Edmund Andros Why are each of these people important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Nathaniel Bacon, Sir Edmund Andros, and Jonathan Edwards. Nathaniel Bacon was a Virginia planter who led a rebellion against the Royal Governor William Berkeley in 1676. Bacon was protesting the inability of Berkeley to protect settlers on the frontier from Native American attacks. After initial success, Bacon died and Berkeley reasserted control over Virginia.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Boston Massacre Albany Congress Stamp Act Congress Boston Tea Party First Continental Congress Years: 1754 1765 1770 1773 1774
items.answer: The Albany Congress was convened in 1754 to address western settlement and the issues this raised with Native Americans. The Stamp Act Congress was held in 1765 to protest the Stamp Act and lobby for its repeal. The Boston Massacre took place in 1770 as British sentries fired into a crowd of unruly American colonists.

items.question: Distinguish between the roles played by George Washington, the Marquis de Montcalm, and William Pitt in the French and Indian War. Why were each of these men important?
items.answer: In 1754, Governor Robert Dinwiddie of Virginia sent George Washington, a young militia officer, to evict the French from Fort Duquesne, which they had built on the site of present day Pittsburgh. Washington was overwhelmed and defeated. He served bravely with General Edward Braddock in 1755 and helped rally the survivors of that general’s defeat.

items.question: Why was this fort important? What does it tell you about warfare in America during the eighteenth century?
items.answer: In the eighteenth century, there were few roads in America. The easiest and fastest way to get around was by water. Lake Champlain was important because it provided an invasion route to and from Canada. Forts on the lake helped control this strategic waterway for the French, British, and later, the Americans. The French Fort Carillon was renamed Ticonderoga after it was captured by the British in 1759.

items.question: Place the following groups of colonists in chronological order: minutemen, Sons of Liberty, Committees of Correspondence. Why were these groups important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Sons of Liberty, Committees of Correspondence, minutemen. All these were groups of Americans resisting the policies of the British government. The Sons of Liberty were organized by Sam Adams in 1765 to resist the Stamp Act. The Sons of Liberty remained active after the Stamp Act crisis.

items.question: What point is Leonard making? Why is this perspective important?
items.answer: Daniel Leonard was a wealthy and successful lawyer in Massachusetts. He opposed the agitation against Parliament and British policy, and skillfully criticized it in his “Letters,” which were published in a newspaper between December 1774 and April 1775. His writings remind us that many American colonists remained loyal to the British government.

items.question: Many American colonists supported the slogan “no taxation without representation.” The British government argued that the colonists enjoyed “virtual representation.” Distinguish between these two positions. Why was the difference important?
items.answer: Traditionally in English history, kings had to go to parliament to raise taxes, establishing the precedent that taxpayers had to have a say on taxes that affected them. The 1689 English Bill of Rights codified the principle that all taxes had to be approved by Parliament. During the long period of Salutary Neglect, the American colonists became accustomed to paying taxes voted by their legislatures.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Declaration of Independence Alliance with France Battle of Yorktown Battle of Saratoga Second Continental Congress Years: 1775 1776 1777 1778 1781
items.answer: The Second Continental Congress convened in May 1775 and was faced with carrying on the war that had just begun with Great Britain. The Declaration of Independence was adopted on July 4, 1776 (the engrossed copy was signed on August 2). The Battle of Saratoga resulted in the surrender of an entire British army on October 17, 1777.

items.question: Place the following legislative enactments in chronological order: the Northwest Ordinances, the Articles of Confederation, the Treaty of Paris. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is the Articles of Confederation, the Treaty of Paris, the Northwest Ordinances. The Articles of Confederation was a constitution for the United States that the Second Continental Congress submitted to the thirteen states on 1777 and which was finally ratified in 1781.

items.question: Look up “Benedict Arnold” in various online dictionaries. To do a “Benedict Arnold” is to betray or sell out a person or a cause. Who was Benedict Arnold? Why has his name become a synonym for traitor in the United States?
items.answer: During the first years of the Revolutionary War, Benedict Arnold was one of the bravest and most effective combat generals in the Continental Army. He led a heroic march to Canada to Quebec in 1775 and was wounded leading an assault on that British-held city. The next year he prevented a British invasion of the United States from Canada by fighting a naval battle on Lake Champlain.

items.question: Distinguish between the contributions of Thomas Paine and Thomas Jefferson to the Declaration of Independence. Why were they important?
items.answer: Thomas Paine’s pamphlet Common Sense was published in January 1776 and made a powerful case for American independence from Great Britain. Common Sense was a publishing sensation. It had an immense circulation and to this day holds the record for being the best-selling title in American history. Paine’s arguments in his pamphlet helped prepare Americans for independence later in the year.

items.question: What makes Independence Hall a remarkable site in American history?
items.answer: Independence Hall played a pivotal role in American history. It was where Congress met for much of the Revolutionary War. It was the place where George Washington was appointed the commander of the Continental Army, and the Declaration of Independence was signed. In 1787, it was the meeting place where delegates gathered to frame and sign the Constitution of the United States.

items.question: What point is Washington making? Why is this perspective important?
items.answer: Washington in this letter is arguing that the United States needs a strong government for the new nation to become great. Without a strong government the United States will be treated contemptuously by the European powers and might even fall apart. This perspective is important because it reveals the concerns about the weakness of the Articles of Confederation that would eventually result in the calling of the Consti...

items.question: Distinguish between the actions of Massachusetts farmers at Lexington in 1775 and during Shays’ Rebellion in 1786. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: In both 1775 at Lexington, and in 1786 during Shays’ Rebellion, Massachusetts farmers were resisting taxation that they believed was unfair. In 1775, the farmers were standing up to the British government and “no taxation without representation.” In 1786, the rebelling farmers were protesting the tax policies of their own state legislature, which was dominated by merchant interests.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Beginning of the French Revolution The Virginia Plan The XYZ Affair Report on the Public Credit The Whisky Rebellion begins Years: 1787 1789 1790 1794 1798
items.answer: The Virginia Plan, proposing a bicameral national legislature with all representatives allocated by proportional representation, was submitted to the Constitutional Convention in 1787. The French Revolution began in 1789, at the same time as the new American government under the Constitution was getting established.

items.question: Place the following documents in chronological order: the Bill of Rights, the Kentucky and Virginia Resolves, The Federalist Papers. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is The Federalist Papers, the Bill of Rights, the Kentucky and Virginia Resolves. The Federalist Papers were a series of articles published by James Madison, Alexander Hamilton, and John Jay intended to persuade the people of New York to support the proposed Constitution. Over time, these articles became seen as a profound commentary on the Constitution.

items.question: What point is Mercy Otis Warren making? Why is this perspective important?
items.answer: Mercy Otis Warren was the sister of James Otis and the wife of James Warren, both prominent leaders in the resistance to British policies. During the Revolution she produced various writings supportive of the Patriot cause. Warren later wrote one of the first histories of the American Revolution. Warren was an anti-Federalist who opposed the ratification of the new Constitution.

items.question: Martha Ballard was a midwife who lived in Maine. At the age of 50, she began a diary, which she maintained for 27 years until her death. In this diary, Ballard kept a brief record of her daily activities, including visits to women in childbirth and ailing neighbors, and also the comings and goings of family members, friends, and neighbors. The historian Laurel Thatcher Ulrich used the diary to write a biography of Ballard entitled A Midwife’s Tale (1990) that was awarded the Pulitzer Prize and several other awards. Clearly a source like Martha Ballard’s diary is not as easy to read as the public papers and memoirs left by important leaders. Why are sources like this diary important?
items.answer: Sources like Martha Ballard’s diary, if studied carefully, can give historians valuable insights into the lives of ordinary men and women. Martha Ballard’s record of her daily activities is especially useful for shedding light on the lives of women on the American frontier in the late eighteenth century, providing important information on people whose lives were generally ignored by contemporary historians.

items.question: Place the following events in American foreign policy in chronological order: the Quasi-War with France, Jay’s Treaty, the Declaration of Neutrality. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is the Declaration of Neutrality, Jay’s Treaty, the Quasi-War with France. George Washington issued the Declaration of Neutrality in 1793. He hoped that the United States could avoid involvement in the war being waged between the Republic of France and Great Britain and its allies.

items.question: Distinguish between the constitutional ideas of Thomas Jefferson and Alexander Hamilton. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Thomas Jefferson took a strict constructionist view of the Constitution. He believed that the federal government could not take any action that was not explicitly spelled out in the Constitution. Hence he opposed Alexander Hamilton’s plan for a Bank of the United States, because there is nothing in the Constitution about a national bank. Alexander Hamilton took a loose constructionist view of the Constitution.

items.question: Why were these important?
items.answer: Following the Revolutionary War, the British did not evacuate all their forts from what had become the northwestern territories of the United States. The British provided support to the Native Americans who were resisting American efforts to assert control over this region. In 1790 and 1791, two American armies were defeated by the Native Americans as they attempted to march into the Northwest Territory.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Treaty of Ghent Louisiana Purchase Twelfth Amendment Battle of Tippecanoe Second National Bank Years: 1803 1804 1811 1814 1816
items.answer: The Louisiana Purchase occurred in 1803. President Thomas Jefferson purchased the Louisiana Territory from France for $15 million, doubling the size of the United States. The Twelfth Amendment was ratified in 1804. It was designed to avoid the electoral tie between Thomas Jefferson and his running mate Aaron Burr in 1800, and stipulated that voters in the Electoral College vote separately for the president and vice p...

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Non-Intercourse Act, Embargo of 1807, Hartford Convention. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Embargo of 1807, Non-Intercourse Act, Hartford Convention. The Embargo Act was a response to years of British impressment of American sailors, interference with American trade, and the 1807 attack on USS Chesapeake by HMS Leopard. President Thomas Jefferson hoped that an embargo on American trade would persuade the warring European powers to respect American rights.

items.question: What point is Chief Justice John Marshall making in this Supreme Court decision? Why is it important?
items.answer: In the Marbury v. Madison decision, Marshall made the case that since the Constitution is the supreme law of the land, the courts could void laws that conflict with the Constitution. This established the principle of judicial review, giving the courts the power to review the constitutionality of laws. This ruling enhanced the prestige and power of the judiciary.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions on Westward Expansion of Tecumseh and Andrew Jackson. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Tecumseh was a Shawnee war leader and diplomat who in the early nineteenth century attempted to create a tribal confederacy to oppose further American settlement on Native American lands. He made it a principle that the land belonged to all Native Americans, and so no individual or group of individuals could sell parts of it to the U.S. government. Andrew Jackson was a supporter of American westward expansion.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Lewis and Clark Expedition, Era of Good Feelings, Battle of New Orleans. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Lewis and Clark Expedition, Battle of New Orleans, Era of Good Feelings. President Thomas Jefferson sent Captain Meriwether Lewis and Second Lieutenant William Clark on an expedition to explore the Louisiana Territory. Their journey lasted from May 1804 to September 1806.

items.question: What point is Adams making in this passage of his history? What widespread view of American life does this passage reflect?
items.answer: Adams is making the point that most Americans worked very hard in the early nineteenth century. They made more money than people in Europe, but had to deal with harsher living conditions. This ties into the traditional view that if you work hard in America, you can make your fortune. One of the most famous manifestations of this were the books for children written by Horatio Alger in the late nineteenth century.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Monroe Doctrine Indian Removal Act Missouri Compromise Nullification Crisis Completion of the Erie Canal Years: 1820 1823 1825 1830 1832
items.answer: The Missouri Compromise was designed to keep a balance between free and slave states. In 1820, Missouri was admitted as a slave state, and Maine as a free state. The compromise, engineered by Henry Clay, drew a line through the Louisiana Territory; areas north of the line would become free states and those south of the line would become slave states.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Bank War, Specie Circular, Panic of 1837. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Bank War, Specie Circular, Panic of 1837. Henry Clay saw the Second Bank of the United States as a centerpiece of his American System. In 1832, as he prepared to run for the presidency, he attempted to have its charter renewed early by Congress. President Andrew Jackson opposed the bank as a tool of special interests. He vetoed the rechartering bill.

items.question: Why was the Trail of Tears important?
items.answer: The Trail of Tears was the culmination of efforts by settlers to acquire the lands lived on by Native Americans in the Eastern United States. The Cherokee tribe fought back in court. In the 1831 case Cherokee Nation v. Georgia, Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the Cherokee were a “domestic dependent nation,” not a foreign state, so the Court could not hear the case; a year later, Worcester v. Georgia (1832) ruled that Georgia’s laws had no force on Cherokee land.

items.question: Distinguish between the ideas of Henry Clay and Andrew Jackson on the economy and government. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Following in the tradition of Alexander Hamilton, Henry Clay believed that the government could play a role in promoting economic growth. His “American System” called for a high protective tariff to encourage the growth of American industry, a Bank of the United States to provide credit and facilitate business transactions, and government support for internal improvements like roads and canals to help businessmen and...

items.question: The Election of 1840 is remembered for the hoopla associated with its electioneering rather than any political issues. Give examples of the creative use of political image-making in this election. Why is this important?
items.answer: In the election of 1840, the Whig Party was determined to win the presidency. Looking for their own Andrew Jackson, they nominated William Henry Harrison, another aging hero of the War of 1812. They came up with a brilliant campaign slogan that reminded voters of Harrison’s 1811 victory over the Indians, as well as his vice presidential running mate, John Tyler—“Tippecanoe and Tyler Too!” Instead of stressing a polit...

items.question: What early nineteenth-century religious phenomenon is Finney referring to? Why was it important?
items.answer: Charles Grandison Finney was one of the greatest preachers of the Second Great Awakening. The Second Great Awakening was a Protestant religious revival movement that began in the 1790s and persisted through the 1830s. This revival emphasized a more personal and emotional religious experience.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Gag Rule, Nat Turner’s Rebellion, the American Colonization Society. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is American Colonization Society, Nat Turner’s Rebellion, Gag Rule. The American Colonization Society was an antislavery society founded in 1817. Members of the society believed that blacks and whites could not live together peacefully in the United States and worked to send freed slaves to new homes in Africa. In 1831, Nat Turner led a bloody slave revolt in Virginia.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: The Mexican War The Alamo The California Gold Rush The Admission of Texas into the Union The Fugitive Slave Act Years: 1836 1845 1846 1848 1850
items.answer: The Battle of the Alamo took place in March 1836 as part of the Texan War of Independence. After a period of independence as the Lone Star Republic, Texas was admitted to the Union in 1845. The Mexican War began in 1846 as Mexican forces challenged the American claim for the southern border of Texas. California was part of the territory won from Mexico during the war.

items.question: Distinguish between Manifest Destiny and the Wilmot Proviso. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Manifest Destiny was a term coined by the Democratic journalist John O’Sullivan in 1845. It referred to the belief that it was the God-given mission of the United States to expand across the continent to the Pacific Ocean. Manifest Destiny appealed to both Northerners and Southerners. In the election of 1844, the Democratic presidential candidate James K.

items.question: Why was the Seneca Falls Women’s Rights Convention important?
items.answer: The Seneca Falls Women’s Rights Convention took place on July 19–20, 1848. It was attended by such well-known activists as Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott. The African American abolitionist Frederick Douglass was also one of the attendees. The convention issued a Declaration of Sentiments that called for the right of women to vote. The convention helped spur further discussion of women’s rights.

items.question: What point is Chief Justice Roger B. Taney making in this Supreme Court decision? Why is this important?
items.answer: Dred Scott was a Missouri slave who sued for his freedom because his master had taken him for a time to live in free parts of the United States. Chief Justice Roger Taney and the Supreme Court ruled that African Americans, whatever their legal status, could not be citizens. The Court also ruled that Congress could not prohibit slavery in the federal territories.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Harper’s Ferry Raid of John Brown, “Bleeding Kansas,” Kansas-Nebraska Act. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Kansas-Nebraska Act, “Bleeding Kansas,” the Harpers Ferry Raid of John Brown. The 1854 Kansas-Nebraska Act was sponsored by Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois as a way to rapidly organize these western territories and promote a transcontinental railroad based in Chicago.

items.question: Distinguish between the views of Stephen A. Douglas and Abraham Lincoln on the issue of slavery in the western territories. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Stephen Douglas ran for reelection to the U.S. Senate as a Democrat in 1858. His Republican opponent was Abraham Lincoln. During the political campaign, Douglas and Lincoln debated at seven locations in Illinois. Douglas defended his belief in popular sovereignty, holding that the citizens of a territory should be able to decide whether they wanted slavery or not.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation Crittenden Plan Draft Riots in New York City South Carolina Secedes from the Union Sherman’s March to the Sea Years: 1860 1861 1862 1863 1864
items.answer: South Carolina responded to the election of Abraham Lincoln as president by seceding from the Union in December 1860. The Crittenden Plan, proposed by Senator John Crittenden of Kentucky in December 1860 and debated through early 1861, was his effort to save the Union through a compromise. He called for the federal government to guarantee the future of slavery where it already existed and for a return to the Missouri Compromise line in the west, with it being extended all th...

items.question: Place the following military events in chronological order: Fort Sumter, Appomattox, Battle of Gettysburg. Why are these military events important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Fort Sumter, Battle of Gettysburg, Appomattox. Fort Sumter was a federal fort in Charleston Harbor. The Confederate decision to bombard the fort into surrender started the fighting in the Civil War. The Battle of Gettysburg took place on July 1–3, 1863. The Federal Army of the Potomac under General George Meade defeated General Robert E.

items.question: Go onto the Internet and visit Civil War reenacting websites. Look at videos of Civil War reenactors on Why is Civil War reenacting so popular? Is this something that you would like to do? Do you find this inappropriate?
items.answer: Civil War reenacting is very popular because it allows people to re-create aspects of one of the most dramatic and important events in American history. Civil War reenactors take pride in their historical heritage, and honor the fighters on both the Northern and Southern sides. While men can dress as soldiers, many women take part in Civil war reenactments, wearing 1860s costumes.

items.question: What point is Congressman Vallandigham making? Why is his perspective important?
items.answer: Congressman Clement Vallandigham was a leading Northern Democratic opponent of the Civil War. Northern Democrats who opposed the war were known as Copperheads. President Abraham Lincoln took vigorous action against these Southern sympathizers. Over 14,000 were jailed without trial. President Lincoln suspended the writ of habeas corpus to keep some of these individuals in prison indefinitely.

items.question: Place the following military events in chronological order: Fall of Atlanta, Battle of Shiloh, Battle of Vicksburg. Why are these military events important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Battle of Shiloh, Battle of Vicksburg, Fall of Atlanta. The Battle of Shiloh was a major battle that took place in the western theater of the war on April 6–7, 1862. General Ulysses S. Grant repulsed a Confederate attack in a hard-fought battle that badly mauled his army.

items.question: Distinguish between the military approaches of the Federal commanders George McClellan and Ulysses S. Grant. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: General George McClellan wanted to fight a limited war. He wanted to restore the Union, but did not want to interfere with Southern institutions like slavery. As a general, he was very cautious and slow, and hoped to outmaneuver his enemies rather than engaging in bloody, head-on battles. General Ulysses S.

items.question: What is Whitman’s perspective on what he sees? Why is this important?
items.answer: Walt Whitman was shocked by the conditions of the hospital treating men wounded at the Battle of Fredericksburg, which took place December 11–15, 1862. The place that he visited was probably a triage point, treating the most badly wounded. Whitman realized that the people running the hospital were doing the best that they could.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Thirteenth Amendment Wade-Davis Act Ten Percent Plan Impeachment of President Andrew Johnson Tenure of Office Act Years: 1863 1864 1865 1867 1868
items.answer: President Abraham Lincoln proposed his Ten Percent Plan for reconstructing the Union in 1863. When ten percent of registered voters in a former Confederate state swore allegiance to the federal government, they could form a new state government. The Wade-Davis Bill was a Radical Republican measure passed by Congress in 1864.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Reconstruction Act, Compromise of 1877, Fifteenth Amendment. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Reconstruction Act, Fifteenth Amendment, Compromise of 1877. The Reconstruction Act was passed by the Radical Republican–dominated Congress in 1867. It divided the former Confederacy into five military districts, each governed by an army general. If former Confederate states were to form new governments, they had to give freedmen equal rights and allow them to vote.

items.question: D. W. Griffith’s 1915 film The Birth of a Nation is an epic recounting of the Civil War and Reconstruction. This was the first great American feature film, and for many technical and artistic reasons it is a landmark in the history of cinema. Unfortunately, Griffith’s film was controversial even in 1915 for its portrayal of Reconstruction. The heroes at the end of the movie are members of the Ku Klux Klan rescuing white Southerners from freedmen and carpetbaggers. The film can be seen in whole or in part at What does this film tell us about changes in our understanding of Reconstruction? How does it illustrate changes in our understanding of race relations?
items.answer: D. W. Griffith based the latter part of The Birth of a Nation on The Clansman (1905), a racist novel by Thomas F. Dixon, Jr., which celebrated the Ku Klux Klan. The son of a former Confederate officer, Griffith was not sensitive to the appalling racism of his source material.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of President Andrew Johnson and the Radical Republicans on Reconstruction. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: President Andrew Johnson attempted to follow what he thought was Abraham Lincoln’s approach to Reconstruction. He wanted to allow the Southern states to be reorganized on lenient terms. Aside from ex-Confederate political and military leaders, and the largest plantation owners, he was willing to offer pardons to former rebels willing to swear their allegiance to the federal government.

items.question: What does Barton reveal about attitudes among the freedmen shortly after the conclusion of the Civil War? Why is this important?
items.answer: Clara Barton’s congressional testimony reveals that there was a great deal of confusion among freedmen shortly after the Civil War. They were not getting good information from their former masters and were subject to conflicting rumors, such as the possibility of being re-enslaved because of the death of Abraham Lincoln.

items.question: Why was the Tuskegee Institute important?
items.answer: The Tuskegee Institute was founded by Booker T. Washington in 1881. Washington was a former slave who believed that the best way forward for African Americans was through economic self-reliance. His school taught students practical skills in farming and the trades. Students built many of the early buildings at Tuskegee. The school also prepared teachers to take knowledge back to their fellow African Americans.

items.question: What is the distinction between a carpetbagger and a scalawag? Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: A carpetbagger was a Northerner who moved to the South after the Civil War. Many were looking for economic opportunity. Others took part in the politics of Reconstruction, playing an important role in the Republican party in the Southern states. Scalawags were Southerners who cooperated with the Republican Reconstruction governments.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Battle of the Little Bighorn Homestead Act Dawes Act Timber and Stone Act Ghost Dance Years: 1862 1876 1878 1887 1890
items.answer: The federal government encouraged Western settlement. The 1862 Homestead Act granted 160 acres of land to a settler willing to farm it for five years. The Battle of the Little Bighorn took place on June 25–26, 1876. A large force of Sioux and Northern Cheyenne defeated a detachment of U.S. cavalry commanded by Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer. Custer and 267 of his men were killed.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Sherman Antitrust Act, completion of the transcontinental railroad, Interstate Commerce Act. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is completion of the transcontinental railroad, Interstate Commerce Act, Sherman Antitrust Act. The Central Pacific and Union Pacific Railroads met at Promontory Summit, Utah, on May 10, 1869. The railroads became a major driver of Western settlement and were vital to the economic interests of Western farmers.

items.question: What does Lease reveal about the perspective of many women living on Western farms in 1891? Why is this perspective important?
items.answer: Mary E. Lease was a fiery spokeswoman for the Farmers’ Alliances and later the Populist Party. She expressed the concerns of Western farmers who were being squeezed by falling prices, and often found themselves unable to pay their mortgages. These farmers blamed their predicament on business monopolies and the gold standard, which contributed to a tighter money supply.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of William Jennings Bryan and William McKinley on the currency issue in the election of 1896. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: William Jennings Bryan was a former congressman from Nebraska who captured the 1896 Democratic presidential nomination by giving a speech at the convention in which he declared, “You shall not crucify mankind upon a cross of gold!” Bryan was a spokesman for the Western farmers who believed that their economic situation was being ruined by tariffs that made prices for goods higher, and the gold standard with its tight...

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: invention of barbed wire, the first “long drive” of cattle, the opening of “Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show.” Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is the first “long drive” of cattle, the invention of barbed wire, and the opening of “Buffalo Bill’s Wild West Show.” The first “long drive” of cattle took place in 1866, when Texas ranchers banded together and drove their herds to the railhead at Sedalia, Missouri. From there the cattle could be shipped to Chicago and Eastern markets.

items.question: Why did the U.S. government honor the Homestead Act with a national monument?
items.answer: The Homestead National Monument was created in 1936 on the site of the farm of Daniel Freeman at Beatrice, Nebraska. Freeman was one of the first people to take advantage of the 1862 Homestead Act, submitting his claim a few minutes after midnight on January 1, 1863. The Homestead Act played an important part in the settlement of the West as many thousands of people took advantage of its provisions to obtain land.

items.question: On July 12, 1893, a young scholar named Frederick Jackson Turner gave an address to a meeting of the American Historical Association at the World Columbian Exposition in Chicago. His talk was entitled “The Significance of the Frontier in American History.” Here Turner laid the foundation for his famous “Frontier Thesis,” which argued that the frontier experience was the most important force shaping American life. He wrote, “The frontier is the line of most rapid and effective Americanization. American social development has been continually beginning over again on the frontier. This perennial rebirth, this fluidity of American life, this expansion westward with its new opportunities, its continuous touch with the simplicity of primitive society, furnish the forces dominating American character . …” Turner’s thesis made him one of the most influential historians in American history. Why did Turner’s view of Western history prove so compelling to his contemporaries?
items.answer: For all of American history up through the late nineteenth century, there had been a frontier offering Americans a chance at a new life. Following the 1890 census, the Census Bureau announced that there no longer was a continuous American frontier. This occurred just as the United States was becoming a great industrial power, with more and more Americans living in cities.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Opening of Ellis Island to process immigrants on the East Coast Knights of Labor founded Coxey’s Army Haymarket Square bombing Chinese Exclusion Act Years: 1869 1882 1886 1892 1894
items.answer: The Knights of Labor was founded in 1869. The Knights of Labor was a union that was open to all workers. The 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act prohibited the immigration of all Chinese laborers. This act was a response to anti-Chinese feeling in California and elsewhere. The Haymarket Square bombing took place on May 4, 1886, in Chicago, Illinois. As police arrived to break up a labor rally, someone threw a bomb at them.

items.question: What is the perspective of AFL president Samuel Gompers in this passage? Why is this perspective important?
items.answer: Samuel Gompers was president of the American Federation of Labor, which was composed of unions serving skilled workers. In 1894, the American Railway Union went on strike to protest conditions at the Pullman Company, which made railroad sleeping cars. Union members refused to work on trains carrying Pullman cars. This caused chaos on the railroads. The federal government intervened against the strike.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Looking Backward, by Edward Bellamy; How the Other Half Lives, by Jacob Riis; Progress and Poverty, by Henry George. Why are these books important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Progress and Poverty, by Henry George; Looking Backward, by Edward Bellamy; How the Other Half Lives, by Jacob Riis. George’s Progress and Poverty (1879) attempted to explain why poverty persisted in a time of technological progress. George argued that landowners benefitted disproportionately from social progress, enabling them to charge higher rents, hurting wage-earners.

items.question: Why has the Statue of Liberty become such an important symbol?
items.answer: The Statue of Liberty, or Liberty Enlightening the World, was conceived of as a gift of the French people to the United States. It was designed by Frederic Auguste Bartholdi and was constructed by Gustave Eiffel. Americans paid for the statue’s pedestal, with the money being raised by subscription. The statue was dedicated October 28, 1886.

items.question: In 1873, Mark Twain and Charles Dudley Warner published a novel entitled The Gilded Age. The novel was a satire of contemporary America, condemning what the authors saw as a postwar riot of greed and public corruption. The title came from Shakespeare: “To gild refined gold, to paint the lily … is wasteful and ridiculous excess.” Twain and Warner achieved something unusual for novelists; they gave a name to a period of history. Why is the period of the late nineteenth century in the United States called the “Gilded Age”?
items.answer: The late nineteenth century in the United States is called the Gilded Age because it was a time of extremes. Businessmen and industrialists made enormous fortunes while many American lived in poverty. It was a time of intense political participation by many Americans but also a time of widespread political corruption, with political machines dominating many localities.

items.question: Distinguish between vertical integration and horizontal integration. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Vertical integration and horizontal integration refer to ways in which late nineteenth-century companies structured their production. Vertical integration refers to a company controlling every phase of production from the acquisition of raw materials through manufacturing, to marketing and distribution. Horizontal integration involves a company controlling production by purchasing or merging with competitors.

items.question: Lord Bryce was a British analyst of American political institutions. What late nineteenth-century political phenomenon is he discussing here?
items.answer: Lord Bryce in this passage is referring to the increasing prevalence of political machines in late nineteenth-century America. Most, though not all, political machines were located in large cities. Political machines were run by bosses, most of whom, as Bryce notes, preferred to operate behind the scenes, though some bosses held elective office.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Spanish-American War Purchase of Alaska from Russia Overthrow of the Kingdom of Hawaii Platt Amendment Publication of The Influence of Sea Power upon History Years: 1867 1890 1893 1898 1901
items.answer: The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867. Unaware of Alaska’s potential resources, many critics termed the purchase “Seward’s Folly” after Secretary of State William H. Seward. Captain Alfred Thayer Mahan’s The Influence of Sea Power upon History was published in 1890.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Great White Fleet, Open Door Note, Boxer Rebellion. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Open Door Note, Boxer Rebellion, Great White Fleet. Secretary of State John Hay sent his first Open Door Note to the other great powers on September 6, 1899. He proposed that the powers allow all countries to trade in China without interference. This became the foundation of the U.S. Open Door policy in China.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of supporters and opponents of imperialism following the Spanish-American War. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: With victory in the Spanish-American War, Americans had to decide what to do about the Philippines after Commodore George Dewey won the Battle of Manila Bay. Supporters of a new American imperial role in the world believed that the United States should claim the Philippines. Theodore Roosevelt believed that the island chain offered the United States commercial advantages in the Asian market.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Roosevelt Corollary, acquisition of the Panama Canal Zone, Dollar Diplomacy. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is acquisition of the Panama Canal Zone, Roosevelt Corollary, Dollar Diplomacy. The United States wanted to construct a canal through the isthmus of Panama connecting the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. In 1903, when a treaty purchasing a canal zone from Colombia fell through, President Theodore Roosevelt supported a revolution that made Panama independent.

items.question: Leonard Wood was Theodore Roosevelt’s partner in creating the 1st Volunteer Cavalry, the famous “Rough Riders.” During the Spanish-American War he was rapidly promoted, and after the conflict he became the military governor of Cuba. What is Wood’s perspective on his role as military governor? What insight does this give us into American imperial attitudes?
items.answer: Leonard Wood saw the role of the U.S. Army as supporting the Cuban people as they created civil government after years of rule by Spain. As governor of Cuba, Wood not only fostered the beginnings of democratic institutions, he also launched a public health campaign that greatly reduced the dangers posed by diseases like yellow fever. Wood is seen as a sort of Progressive reformer who operated overseas.

items.question: Go to this Library of Congress page on the Panama Canal: This page features a silent film on the making of the Panama Canal that was produced in the 1920s. What perspective does the film take toward Theodore Roosevelt and his efforts to build a canal? What is the perspective of the film on the American role in building the canal?
items.answer: The film takes a very positive perspective on Theodore Roosevelt’s role in building the Panama Canal. Roosevelt is seen as completing Christopher Columbus’s mission of discovery and exploration, looking for a route to the Indies. The canal is seen as a triumph of American energy, enterprise, and engineering. The film sees the canal as a measure of the U.S. position at the forefront of progress.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Woodrow Wilson elected president Theodore Roosevelt elected president William Howard Taft elected president The Hepburn Act The foundation of the NAACP Years: 1904 1906 1908 1909 1912
items.answer: Vice President Theodore Roosevelt became president when William McKinley was assassinated in 1901. He was elected president in his own right in 1904, defeating the Democratic candidate Judge Alton B. Parker. The 1906 Hepburn Act gave the Interstate Commerce Commission greater regulatory authority over railroads, including the power to set maximum railroad rates.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Pure Food and Drug Act, Federal Trade Commission Act, Clayton Antitrust Act. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Pure Food and Drug Act, Federal Reserve Act, Clayton Antitrust Act. The 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act gave the U.S. government the authority to regulate foods and drugs for purity and safety. The act required manufacturers to list active ingredients on labels and gave the Bureau of Chemistry (the forerunner of the FDA) the power to test products. Reformers like Dr.

items.question: What problem is La Follette highlighting in this passage? Why is La Follette’s perspective important?
items.answer: After serving three terms in the U.S. House of Representatives, Robert La Follette became concerned about the power wielded by business interests in his state of Wisconsin. He organized an insurgent group within the Wisconsin Republican party, and in 1900 was elected governor. In office, La Follette enacted a series of reforms, including greater regulation of railroad rates. In 1906, La Follette moved on to the U.S.

items.question: Look up the definition of muckraker. The term received its modern meaning from President Theodore Roosevelt in a speech on April 14, 1906. While Roosevelt approved of journalistic exposures of corruption, he cautioned that too many reporters could not tear themselves away from raking muck, like a character in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (1678). Despite, Roosevelt’s criticism, the term muckraker soon became a source of pride to investigative journalists. Why were muckrakers important in the Progressive Era?
items.answer: Muckrakers played an important role in publicizing corporate abuses, political malfeasance, and other social problems during the Progressive Era. They helped mobilize public opinion behind progressive reforms. Although muckrakers published in a variety of venues, some periodicals such as McClure’s Magazine became famous for their investigative journalism. Famous muckrakers include Ida M.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Ballinger-Pinchot Affair, Northern Securities Case, Sixteenth Amendment. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Northern Securities Case, Ballinger-Pinchot Affair, and Sixteenth Amendment. The Northern Securities Company was organized in 1901 by James J. Hill, E. H. Harriman, and J. P. Morgan, and controlled a number of railroads. In 1902, President Theodore Roosevelt directed the Justice Department to sue for the dissolution of the company under the Sherman Antitrust Act.

items.question: This passage is a newspaper account of the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire. Because of poor safety conditions, including doors to stairwells that had been chained shut to prevent possible thefts, 146 workers, mostly young women, died when fire swept through the Triangle Shirtwaist Company on the eighth, ninth, and tenth floors of the Asch Building in New York City. What were some of the consequences of this tragedy?
items.answer: The disastrous Triangle Shirtwaist Fire shocked the nation in 1911. It had immediate consequences in New York. After an investigation, new workplace safety laws were enacted in New York. The New York legislature also passed a bill to shorten workers’ hours. These bills became models for other states. The tragedy also proved a spur to unionization.

items.question: Distinguish between Theodore Roosevelt’s New Nationalism and Woodrow Wilson’s New Freedom. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Theodore Roosevelt began promulgating his New Nationalism in 1910, and it became the basis of his run for the presidency in 1912 as the candidate of the Progressive (Bull Moose) party. Roosevelt called for an expanded role for the federal government in regulating business and the economy.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Zimmermann Telegram Outbreak of War in Europe Treaty of Versailles Announcement of the Fourteen Points Sussex Pledge Years: 1914 1916 1917 1918 1919
items.answer: World War I broke out in August 1914, following a diplomatic crisis precipitated by the assassination of the Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand. The 1916 Sussex Pledge was a reaction of the Imperial German government to American criticism of its campaign of unrestricted submarine warfare against the British and French. The Germans had recently sunk the Sussex, with the loss of 50 lives.

items.question: When he asked Congress to declare war on Imperial Germany, what did Woodrow Wilson believe the United States should be fighting for? Why is this important?
items.answer: President Woodrow Wilson’s War Message to Congress envisioned a very idealistic war. The United States went to war because of the German submarine campaign and questions of the freedom of the seas. Wilson was interested in ensuring the freedom of the seas, but he also wanted to see a new, more democratic world emerge from the conflict. He embodied his ideas on a just peace in his Fourteen Points.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Lusitania, Meuse-Argonne Offensive, Lever Food and Fuel Control Act. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Lusitania, Lever Food and Fuel Control Act, Meuse-Argonne Offensive. The Lusitania was a British passenger liner that was sunk by a German submarine off the coast of Ireland on May 7, 1915. 1,198 passengers and crew lost their lives, including 128 Americans. This sinking outraged American public opinion and led to a diplomatic crisis with Germany.

items.question: What was the purpose of Congress in passing the Sedition Act? What does this tell us about the United States during World War I?
items.answer: The 1918 Sedition Act was an expansion of the 1917 Espionage Act. It was designed to quell dissent and actions that might interfere with the war effort. It was also intended to end vigilante actions by citizens against supposed traitors by giving the government the power to prosecute them. The law reflected the widespread intolerance for dissenting viewpoints on the war.

items.question: Distinguish between the supporters of the League of Nations and “reservationists.” Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: President Woodrow Wilson and supporters of the League of Nations believed that the international organization would prevent any more conflicts like World War I. Operating under the principle of collective security, member states would act to resolve international disputes and oppose unprovoked aggressions.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Washington Disarmament Conference Start of Prohibition Lindbergh Flight across the Atlantic Stock Market Crash Scopes Trial Years: 1920 1921 1925 1927 1929
items.answer: A constitutional amendment to introduce national prohibition was passed by Congress in 1917 and was ratified by the states in 1919. The Volstead Act to enforce prohibition passed Congress on October 28, 1919. Prohibition went into effect on January 17, 1920. The Washington Disarmament Conference convened on November 12, 1921.

items.question: The writer F. Scott Fitzgerald entitled a 1922 collection of short stories Tales of the Jazz Age. This helped popularize a term that became associated with the 1920s. Why is the “Jazz Age” an appropriate name for the decade that followed the conclusion of World War I?
items.answer: The name “Jazz Age” is appropriate for the 1920s in part because this was a time when jazz music became very popular. Both African American musicians like Louis Armstrong and white jazz musicians such as the bandleader Paul Whiteman enjoyed a great deal of success. Serious composers like George Gershwin wrote music heavily influenced by jazz.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: execution of Sacco and Vanzetti, National Origins Act, Palmer Raids. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Palmer Raids, National Origins Act, execution of Sacco and Vanzetti. Attorney General A. Mitchell Palmer launched the Palmer Raids between November 1919 and January 1920. These were a response to terrorist bombings. The raids rounded up thousands of left-wing radicals, and 500 were deported. This was a major moment in the first Red Scare.

items.question: What is President Coolidge’s point in this speech? What does this say about the governing philosophy of the Republican presidential administrations of the 1920s?
items.answer: In this speech, Coolidge is making the point that decreases in government spending benefit ordinary Americans by reducing taxes, which allows them to keep more of their money. Like his predecessor Warren G. Harding, Coolidge believed in limited government. Both Harding and Coolidge cut government spending and lowered taxes.

items.question: Why did Lindbergh become an international hero? What was the significance of his achievement?
items.answer: In May 1927, Charles Lindbergh became the first person to make a solo flight across the Atlantic in his plane The Spirit of St. Louis. Lindbergh was honored for his courage and skill in singlehandedly accomplishing a feat that had cost other pilots their lives. Lindbergh increased the esteem of his contemporaries through his modesty and unwillingness to financially capitalize on his achievement.

items.question: Distinguish between the views of Herbert Hoover and Alfred “Al” Smith concerning Prohibition in the 1928 presidential election. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Governor Alfred “Al” Smith of New York was the Democratic nominee for president in 1928. A native of New York City, and in his early career associated with the Tammany Hall political machine, Smith vehemently opposed Prohibition. Herbert Hoover, the Republican nominee, expressed some support for Prohibition, calling it an “experiment noble in purpose.” Hoover, famous as a philanthropist and energetic public servant,...

items.question: What social development is Frederick Lewis Allen describing in an early popular history of the 1920s? Why was this important?
items.answer: Frederick Lewis Allen is describing changes in the behavior of young women in the 1920s. Women had received the vote in 1920, but one of the most conspicuous developments of the decade was the growing social freedom of women. Women shed their corsets and long, heavy dresses and embraced makeup. The “flapper,” with her bobbed hair, short dress, and mannish figure became the symbol of the age.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: End of Prohibition Hawley-Smoot Tariff Scottsboro Boys Trial Reconstruction Finance Corporation Formation of the Congress of Industrial Organization (CIO) Years: 1930 1931 1932 1933 1935
items.answer: The 1930 Hawley-Smoot Tariff was intended to protect American industries and jobs by making foreign goods more expensive. It had the unintended effect of leading other countries to increase their tariffs, hurting foreign trade and Americans who worked in industries that exported goods. The 1931 Scottsboro Boys Trial involved nine African American teenagers who were convicted of raping two white women on a train.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Social Security Act, Justice Reorganization Bill, National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA). Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA), Social Security Act, Justice Reorganization Bill. The 1933 NIRA was a centerpiece of the First New Deal. The NIRA attempted to restore industrial prosperity by encouraging industries to set standards for prices and competition, while also protecting the rights of workers.

items.question: Mrs. Henderson lived in Oklahoma. What phenomenon is she describing? Why was it important?
items.answer: Mrs. Henderson’s letter is referring to the effects of the Dust Bowl. Beginning in 1934, a series of droughts in the 1930s dried out soil that had been exposed by years of farming in the Lower Plains states and produced immense clouds of dust. Many people lost their farms. By 1940, 3.5 million people moved away from the affected area.

items.question: Distinguish between the approaches of Herbert Hoover and Franklin D. Roosevelt in combating the Great Depression. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: It is not true that President Herbert Hoover did nothing to help people during the Great Depression. He actively used the power of the federal government to combat the depression. He cut taxes and launched public works to provide employment. He signed legislation such as the Hawley-Smoot Tariff and helped create the Reconstruction Finance Corporation (RFC) to pump money into the economy by lending money to banks and...

items.question: Why was Franklin D. Roosevelt so effective as a leader?
items.answer: Although Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal failed to end the Great Depression, he did build a New Deal Coalition that endured for many decades. Born to wealth, as his home indicates, FDR had a capacity to empathize and communicate with ordinary Americans. Some scholars attribute this to his long struggle with the polio that crippled his legs.

items.question: Robert Penn Warren’s great novel All the King’s Men was about a southern politician loosely based on Louisiana’s Huey P. Long. In the passage above, the novel’s narrator Jack Burden reflects on Willie Stark, his former boss. Why would a figure like Huey P. Long evoke such mixed emotions?
items.answer: Huey P. Long served as governor of Louisiana from 1928–1932, and as U.S. senator from 1932–1935. Long built a political machine in Louisiana that made him the virtual dictator of the state. He remained very popular in Louisiana because he spoke up for the poor, built a string of charity hospitals, and expanded schools, with free textbooks for schoolchildren. As an ambitious senator, Long aimed for the presidency.

items.question: What point is the labor leader John L. Lewis making in the passage above? Why did he feel that he had to make this point?
items.answer: President Franklin D. Roosevelt and his New Deal provided increased legal support to the labor movement. The 1935 Wagner Act affirmed the right of workers to unionize and bargain collectively. The Wagner Act also outlawed certain labor practices and established the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) to enforce the labor laws. This led to an effort to expand unionization. John L.

items.question: Distinguish between the First and Second New Deals. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: President Franklin D. Roosevelt promoted recovery, relief, and reform in his New Deal Program. The First New Deal of 1933–1934 emphasized recovery and relief, with agencies such as the National Recovery Administration (NRA), Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC), and the Agricultural Adjustment Administration (AAA).

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: First Neutrality Act German Invasion of Poland Lend-Lease Act Destroyers for Bases Agreement Internment Camps for Japanese established Years: 1935 1939 1940 1941 1942
items.answer: The Neutrality Act of 1935 was an effort to keep the United States out of a conflict like World War I. The law established a six-month moratorium on American trade in weapons or military supplies with warring countries. Following the signing of a nonaggression pact with the Soviet Union, Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, beginning World War II.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Battle of the Bulge, Battle of Midway, Battle of Guadalcanal. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Battle of Midway, Battle of Guadalcanal, and Battle of the Bulge. The Battle of Midway, fought June 4–7, 1942, turned the tide of the war in the Pacific Theater. In a battle dominated by aircraft carriers, the Americans sank four Japanese aircraft carriers while losing one aircraft carrier of their own. After this defeat, the Japanese were forced on the defensive.

items.question: What foreign policy position is Senator Nye taking in the passage above? How influential was this perspective?
items.answer: Senator Gerald P. Nye of North Dakota was an influential isolationist. From 1934 to 1936, Nye headed a Senate investigation into the munitions industry to see if prominent American businesses had helped lead the United States into World War I. He played an important role in passing the neutrality laws designed to keep the United States out of another war. Nye opposed American intervention in World War II.

items.question: Why is what happened on December 7, 1941, so important?
items.answer: The World War II Valor in the Pacific National Monument lies above the resting place of the USS Arizona. During the December 7, 1941, Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, the Arizona, an American battleship, was sunk with the loss of 1,177 men. In all, during the Japanese assault, 2,403 Americans were killed and 1,178 were wounded. The United States and Japan disagreed over Japanese conquests in China and Indochina.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Beginning of the draft, G.I. Bill, Revenue Act of 1942. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is beginning of the draft, Revenue Act of 1942, G.I. Bill. In 1940, in response to the security threat posed by the outbreak of World War II and Axis victories, the United States launched a massive rearmament program to build up American defenses. Part of this program was the institution of a draft to build up the army.

items.question: Distinguish between the narrow front and broad front strategies in the European Theater of World War II. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Following the Allied breakout from the D-Day beachhead in July, 1944, a dispute arose over the best way to complete the rout of the German armies and end the war. The Allied armies moved so fast that they began to outrun available supplies, especially gasoline. The British General Bernard Montgomery argued for a narrow front thrust into Germany by his forces.

items.question: Paul Fussell was a distinguished professor of literature and writer, who in his youth had served as an infantry officer in the European Theater of World War II. His essay “Thank God for the Atomic Bomb” was a response to critics who argued that the dropping of the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki was immoral. What is his perspective, and why is it significant?
items.answer: By August 1945, Japan was isolated and objectively beaten. Despite this, the military rulers of Japan declared that they would fight on and were gathering large forces to resist an American invasion. The Americans were preparing Operation Olympic, an assault on the Japanese home islands.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Federal Employee Loyalty Program Winston Churchill’s “Iron Curtain” Speech Start of the Korean War Yalta Conference Establishment of the Communist People’s Republic of China Years: 1945 1946 1947 1949 1950
items.answer: The February 1945 Yalta Conference between President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Josef Stalin discussed postwar conditions in Europe. Stalin promised free elections in Poland, a pledge he later broke. On March 5, 1946, Winston Churchill, now out of office, gave his “Iron Curtain” speech while visiting the United States.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Marshall Plan, NATO, Truman Doctrine. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, NATO. In early 1947, the British told the American government that they could no longer protect Greece and Turkey from Communist threats. In gathering Congressional support to take over for the British, President Harry Truman announced what came to be known as the “Truman Doctrine” on March 12, 1947.

items.question: What foreign policy approach is George F. Kennan advocating? Why is this important?
items.answer: George F. Kennan was an American diplomat with extensive experience in the Soviet Union by the mid-1940s. In his “Long Telegram” sent to Washington on February 22, 1946, and his 1947 Foreign Affairs article, initially published anonymously and signed “X,” Kennan formulated the policy of containment.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of President Harry Truman and Senator Joseph McCarthy regarding Soviet espionage in the United States. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Both President Harry Truman and Senator Joseph McCarthy believed that Soviet spies had infiltrated the American government. Revelations about Soviet spying, including in the atomic bomb program, became public in the late 1940s and early 1950s. President Truman responded to this with his Federal Employee Loyalty program, which established a Loyalty Review Board to sift security risks out of the federal bureaucracy.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Soviet downing of a U-2 plane, Geneva Accords, Sputnik. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Geneva Accords, Sputnik, the Soviet downing of a U-2 plane. The Geneva Accords were announced on July 21, 1954. They were the result of a conference called to determine the future of Indochina. While the conference was ongoing, on May 7, the French were forced to surrender the remains of an army at Dien Bien Phu.

items.question: Why is this site important for understanding the history of the cold war?
items.answer: During the 1950s, the United States began deploying Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles (ICBMs) as part of its nuclear deterrent against the Soviet Union. In the mid-1950s development began on the solid-fuel Minuteman missile. ICBMs, capable of carrying increasingly destructive nuclear warheads, were the most deadly weapons ever created.

items.question: What famous foreign policy theory did President Eisenhower articulate in this news conference? Why is it important?
items.answer: In this news conference President Dwight D. Eisenhower articulated the “Domino Theory.” This argues that, if one country in a region falls to Communism, other neighboring countries will succumb as well, like a line of falling dominoes. This formulation is important because it became an underpinning of American involvement in Indochina in the 1950s and 1960s.

items.question: In the 1960s a new generation of “revisionist” historians questioned cold war orthodoxy and argued against the belief that the Soviet Union was solely responsible for the cold war, instead contending that the United States, pursuing expansive strategic and economic interests, made the dominant contribution to the onset of the struggle. A later generation of “post-revisionist” scholars challenged this interpretation and said that while both superpowers contributed to the coming of the cold war, the “revisionists” downplayed the effects of Soviet policies in precipitating conflict. Why did the disputes between historians of the cold war take on a greater significance than the usual academic debates over the past?
items.answer: The disputes over the origins of the cold war took on greater significance than usual academic debates over the past because they often reflected deep political divisions. The cold war lasted over 40 years. It was still ongoing when many of these historical debates took place. The understanding of the past was thought to have relevance for present and future policy.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Interstate Highway Act Taft-Hartley Act Publication of On the Road Checkers Speech Fair Deal Years: 1947 1949 1952 1956 1957
items.answer: The 1947 Taft-Hartley Act was passed over President Harry Truman’s veto in a brief interval between 1947 and 1949 when the Republicans controlled Congress. The law placed some limits on union activity and required union leaders to declare that they were not Communists. Newly elected President Truman proposed an ambitious program of legislation that he called the Fair Deal in 1949.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of President Harry Truman and South Carolina Governor Strom Thurmond on civil rights in 1948. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: In 1948, facing a strong challenge from the Republicans and New York Governor Thomas E. Dewey, President Harry Truman appealed to African American voters by proposing laws to extend greater civil rights protections to them. At the Democratic Convention, he supported a plank favoring greater civil rights for African Americans. This alienated many Southern Democrats.
