items.question: What social and economic reality is reflected in President Eisenhower’s Second Inaugural?
items.answer: President Eisenhower’s Second Inaugural reflects a widespread American prosperity in the 1950s. Prosperity began after World War II, with unemployment falling to about 4 percent in 1948. With many competitors hobbled by wartime damage, American industry dominated the world. In 1950, American industries produced 6.2 million automobiles, 6.2 million refrigerators, and 14.6 million radios.

items.question: In the 1998 film Pleasantville, the 1950s is presented as a time of repression, especially for African Americans and women. That women were all forced to be housewives is a widespread view of the era. Yet, by 1957 more women were working than during World War II. By 1960, 40 percent of women held jobs. Why does the less-complicated view of women’s roles in the 1950s persist? Why is this important?
items.answer: One reason for the Pleasantville view of women in the 1950s is that the popular culture of the time exalted the role of woman as homemaker. Many women’s magazines, movies, and television shows persistently portrayed women as happy in the home. A good example of this would be the hit sitcom Leave It to Beaver, which first aired in 1957. Critics of this role for women helped shape the current view in the 1960s.

items.question: Why were Levittown and developments like it important?
items.answer: William Levitt was a developer who created seven “Levittowns” in the postwar years. His developments utilized assembly-line construction techniques perfected during World War II to quickly produce communities of largely identical homes that were comfortable and reasonably priced.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Montgomery Bus Boycott, Brown v. Board of Education, Little Rock Nine. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Brown v. Board of Education, Montgomery Bus Boycott, Little Rock Nine. The 1954 Brown v. Board of Education Supreme Court decision was a landmark in the African American struggle for civil rights. The Supreme Court ruled against segregation in schools by declaring that “separate but equal” was illegal.

items.question: What is the perspective of this passage from a news report? Why is it important?
items.answer: The news story from the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reflects a critical attitude toward rock and roll. The new music, being popularized by bands like Bill Haley and his Comets, is seen as encouraging violent behavior. Many adults in the 1950s believed that rock and roll was “devil’s music,” and associated it with immorality.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Bay of Pigs Sit-ins begin Assassination of President John F. Kennedy Cuban Missile Crisis Gulf of Tonkin Resolution Years: 1960 1961 1962 1963 1964
items.answer: Sit-ins as a tactic for civil rights protesters began in 1960. African American students staged a sit-in at a segregated lunch counter at a Greensboro, North Carolina, Woolworth store. In an attempt to overthrow the Communist regime of Fidel Castro in Cuba, the United States landed a force of anti-Castro Cubans at the Bay of Pigs in Cuba on April 17, 1961.

items.question: What is the perspective of Senator Goldwater? Why is it important?
items.answer: Senator Barry Goldwater of Arizona won the Republican nomination for president in 1964. Goldwater was a conservative who rejected the political legacy of the New Deal. He called for a return to limited government and promised a more robust military and diplomatic response to Communist aggression. In the general election Goldwater was heavily defeated by President Lyndon B.

items.question: Distinguish between “Old Left” and “New Left.” Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: The “Old Left” was associated with loyalty to the Communist Party and an approach to politics that emphasized ideological discipline and a hierarchical organization. The young founders of the “New Left” rejected this approach. They stressed “participatory democracy” and individual control of one’s life.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Tet Offensive, Woodstock Music Festival, Medicare. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Medicare, Tet Offensive, and Woodstock Music Festival. Medicare was passed in 1965 as part of President Lyndon B. Johnson’s Great Society. Medicare is a federal program that provides medical insurance to Americans aged 65 and older. The Tet Offensive was a massive series of Communist attacks that were launched all across South Vietnam beginning on January 30, 1968.

items.question: What is the perspective of President Johnson in this passage? Why is it important?
items.answer: In this passage, President Lyndon B. Johnson is defending American involvement in Vietnam. At this point, the United States was supporting South Vietnam against an insurgency being waged by Viet Cong guerillas and soldiers from North Vietnam. In March, Johnson had sent a contingent of Marines into Vietnam to protect the American airbase at Danang.

items.question: How does the memorial capture Americans’ complex feelings about the Vietnam War?
items.answer: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial was designed by a young artist named Maya Lin and was dedicated on November 13, 1982. The design, two long black walls etched with the names of the 58,000 Americans who lost their lives in the Vietnam War, was controversial because some critics thought it was too modest and somber and did not celebrate the achievements of the memorialized servicemen and women.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Fall of South Vietnam Resignation of President Richard Nixon Iran Hostage Crisis begins Roe v. Wade Camp David Accords Years: 1973 1974 1975 1978 1979
items.answer: The 1973 Roe v. Wade Supreme Court decision argued that women had a right to an abortion before fetal viability. This set off a long-standing political battle over abortion. President Richard M. Nixon resigned on August 9, 1974. He was in danger of being impeached for obstruction of justice in the Watergate scandal, and his political situation had become untenable.

items.question: Distinguish between the foreign policy approach of President Richard M. Nixon and his predecessors. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: President Richard M. Nixon was innovative in his foreign policy initiatives. He launched a new phase of the Vietnam War with his policy of “Vietnamization,” which consisted of turning more of the fighting over to the South Vietnamese while gradually pulling out American troops. Nixon supported the South Vietnamese with training, supplies, and a massive bombing campaign.

items.question: What problem is President Carter referring to in this passage? Why is this important?
items.answer: President Jimmy Carter was referring to the energy crisis of the 1970s. The world faced shortages of oil as a result of the Arab Oil Embargo in the aftermath of the 1973 Yom Kippur War and the 1979 Iranian Revolution. In 1973 American drivers for a time had to submit to gas rationing. In 1974, Congress passed a law setting the national speed limit at 55 miles per hour.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Tax Reform Act, Strategic Defense Initiative, INF Treaty. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Strategic Defense Initiative, Tax Reform Act, and INF Treaty. Under President Ronald Reagan Cold War tensions intensified as he accelerated an arms buildup begun under President Jimmy Carter. Reagan also ramped up rhetorical attacks on the Soviet dictatorship.

items.question: What perspective on government does President Reagan express in this passage? Why is this important?
items.answer: President Ronald Reagan believed that prosperity came from Americans pursuing their economic goals as freely as possible from government intervention. To encourage this, Reagan attempted to cut the size of government and turn some services back to the states with his plan for a New Federalism. He also cut tax rates and promoted the policy of deregulation in the energy and transportation industries.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Fall of the Berlin Wall Operation Desert Shield Fall of the Soviet Union Passage of NAFTA Election of Bill Clinton Years: 1989 1990 1991 1992 1993
items.answer: The Berlin Wall was broken down in 1989 as the Soviet Union weakened and the people of Eastern Europe began to overthrow their Soviet-imposed Communist governments. Operation Desert Shield was implemented by President George Herbert Walker Bush to protect Saudi Arabia after Iraq invaded and conquered Kuwait in August 1990.

items.question: President Bush in the passage above expressed the euphoria at the end of the cold war. Americans began to expect a “peace dividend” in the form of decreased defense spending. The scholar Francis Fukuyama published a widely discussed book entitled The End of History and the Last Man (1992) in which he argued that with the demise of Communism, humanity had reached the end of its ideological evolution, and the world would gradually adopt Western liberal democracy. Was Fukuyama’s prediction of an end of ideological struggle borne out by events?
items.answer: The end of the Cold War was a watershed event. The American people wanted to enjoy their “peace dividend” and move in new directions. In the election of 1992, President George Herbert Walker Bush was replaced by the much younger William Jefferson (Bill) Clinton. While scholars debated Francis Fukuyama’s thesis on the “end of history,” most Americans enjoyed the prosperity of the 1990s.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: Kosovo War, Contract with America, Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act. Why are these important?
items.answer: The proper chronological order is Contract with America, Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act, Kosovo War. The 1994 Contract with America was written by Republican congressmen Newt Gingrich and Dick Armey. It was signed by almost all Republican congressional candidates and laid out a detailed platform of objectives, including welfare reform and tax cuts.

items.question: What allegation is President Clinton referring to in this passage? Why is it important?
items.answer: Because of continuing allegations of corruption about a land deal involving the Whitewater Development Corporation during President Bill Clinton’s time as governor of Arkansas, Ken Starr was appointed as an independent counsel to investigate his involvement.

items.question: Distinguish between traditional Democrats in the early 1990s and Bill Clinton’s position as a “New Democrat.” Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: Democrats running as traditional liberals supporting an expansion of government programs to meet social problems lost the elections of 1984 and 1988. This led some Democrats to argue that the party needed to move closer to the political center. In 1985 the Democratic Leadership Council (DLC) was founded to promote this approach.

items.question: In the passage above, journalist John Greenwald notes that before the dotcom stock crash of 2000, enormous fortunes had been made in the emerging industry that serviced the Internet. How did the dotcom boom reflect the larger economy during the 1990s?
items.answer: Overall, the decade of the 1990s was prosperous, with the last years of the decade especially so. Americans benefitted from lower taxes, lower energy prices, and the emergence of new industries like the dotcom companies pioneering the developing Internet. Following the recession of 1992, the unemployment rate fell to 4 percent by the end of the decade.

items.question: Connect the following events with the proper year: Events: Affordable Care Act Hurricane Katrina Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) Invasion of Afghanistan Creation of the Department of Homeland Security Years: 2001 2002 2005 2008 2010
items.answer: The United States attacked Afghanistan on October 7, 2001. The United States invaded Afghanistan to overthrow the Taliban government that was sheltering Osama bin Laden and other Al Qaeda figures implicated in the 9/11 attacks on the United States. President George W. Bush created an Office of Homeland Security shortly after the 9/11 attacks.

items.question: What policy initiative was President Bush promoting in the passage above? Why is it important?
items.answer: In this speech before a Joint Session of Congress, President Bush was arguing for his program of tax cuts. Bush believed that these cuts would stimulate the economy following a recession caused by the collapse of the dotcom boom. Bush secured tax cuts in 2001 and 2003. These cut the highest tax rate to 35 percent. The Bush tax cuts were intended to expire in 2010.

items.question: Place the following in chronological order: President Bush’s “Surge” in Iraq, the ISIS conquest of Mosul, Operation Iraqi Freedom. Why are these important?
items.answer: Following 9/11, the U.S. government and its allies grew concerned about the Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein. They held him to be in noncompliance with UN Security Council Resolutions passed since the Gulf War. President George W. Bush, British Prime Minister Tony Blair, and other leaders believed that Saddam Hussein was stockpiling weapons of mass destruction.

items.question: Distinguish between the positions of 2012 presidential candidates President Barack Obama and Mitt Romney on the issue of gay marriage. Why is this distinction important?
items.answer: On May 9, 2012, President Barack Obama publicly announced support for gay marriage. Former Massachusetts governor Mitt Romney, his Republican opponent in the 2012 presidential election, opposed gay marriage and supported a proposed constitutional amendment to limit marriage to one man and one woman.

items.question: In the passage above, what is President Obama’s perspective on immigration policy? Why is this important?
items.answer: Immigration and immigration reform were contentious political issues during the Bush and Obama Administrations. Immigration reform legislation failed to pass out of Congress. President Barack Obama was reluctant to deport law-abiding illegal immigrants.
